independence.note: This record uses only public external sources discovered in this run plus this worker's clean namespace. Legacy pre_independence state was not used as exploration continuation.

search_bias: Start outside mainstream agent literature: algorithm configuration/selection, parallel scheduling, automated scientific experimentation, software debugging; prefer quantitative primary evidence and extract transferable mechanisms rather than field-specific labels.

candidates.mechanism: Statistical racing: evaluate candidates incrementally and eliminate poor candidates as soon as paired statistical evidence is sufficient, reallocating budget to survivors.
candidates.primary_source: Birattari et al., A Racing Algorithm for Configuring Metaheuristics (2002), https://iridia.ulb.ac.be/~stuetzle/publications/BirStuPaqVar02.pdf
candidates.quantitative_evidence: In 1000 pseudo-trials over 256 configurations, F-Race ended with about 7.9 survivors tested on 77.9 instances on average; a brute-force 'Cheat' comparator used about 19,950 experiments / ~55 h per trial versus 3.5 h available to F-Race, while tests could not reject equivalent selected-result quality at 5% significance. F-Race was also significantly better than two t-test racing baselines at 5%.
candidates.scope: Automatic configuration of MAX-MIN Ant System on generated TSP-like instances; pseudo-trial/resampling design. Do not generalize the exact efficiency ratio beyond this setting.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: For expensive research/evaluation loops, treat candidate mechanisms as a race: use matched tasks/seeds and sequential evidence to stop weak branches early while spending more evaluations on survivors. This is a hypothesis for transfer, not evidence of AGI acceleration.
candidates.confidence: high for original mechanism; medium for transfer

candidates.mechanism: Per-instance algorithm portfolios: keep diverse solvers whose runtimes are imperfectly correlated, predict which solver is best for each instance, and use short pre-solvers for easy cases.
candidates.primary_source: Xu et al., SATzilla-07: The Design and Analysis of an Algorithm Portfolio for SAT (2007), https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hutter/papers/cp07-satzilla.pdf
candidates.quantitative_evidence: On QCP test data, winner-take-all OKsolver averaged 543 CPU s while SATzilla-07 averaged 205 CPU s. On BIG-MIX, SATzilla averaged 154 CPU s versus 407 CPU s for the best single solver and solved 20% more instances within cutoff. On RANDOM it was >3x faster than the best single solver and solved 15% more; on HANDMADE it was >50% faster and solved 11% more. The method explicitly exploited low runtime correlation between pre-solvers (reported r=0.118 on one shared subset).
candidates.scope: SAT solver selection on benchmark distributions with engineered features and trained empirical hardness models; feature-computation overhead included in reported curves.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: Research orchestration may benefit more from retaining genuinely diverse methods and routing each problem/state to a predicted-best method than from converging globally on one dominant procedure. Requires measurable instance features and out-of-sample routing validation.
candidates.confidence: high for original mechanism; medium for transfer

candidates.mechanism: Randomized work stealing: workers with no local work steal ready subproblems from randomly chosen busy workers, yielding decentralized adaptive load balancing.
candidates.quantitative_evidence: For high-parallelism Cilk benchmarks, scheduler speedup exceeded 99% of perfect linear speedup on 32 processors and 95% on 256 processors. Moderately long-thread programs had >90% serial efficiency. Theory bounds expected execution near O(T1/P + Tinf) and communication O(P*Tinf*(1+nd)*Smax) for fully strict computations.
candidates.scope: Fully strict multithreaded computations on Cilk/CM5-era systems; benefits depend on enough parallelism and sufficiently coarse tasks. Very short tasks incur high spawn overhead.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: For parallel research workers, avoid centrally preassigning all subproblems. Maintain local queues and allow idle workers to steal unresolved frontier items, while keeping tasks coarse enough to dominate orchestration overhead. Independence constraints may require stealing only O-blind frontier units.
candidates.confidence: high for original mechanism; medium for transfer

candidates.mechanism: Closed-loop transfer: combine optimization with interpretable supervised models and physics/domain features so each experiment both seeks performance and produces transferable explanatory hypotheses; validate hypotheses with separate perturbation tests.
candidates.primary_source: Angello et al., Closed-loop transfer enables artificial intelligence to yield chemical knowledge, Nature 633, 351-358 (2024), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07892-1
candidates.quantitative_evidence: The campaign characterized about 1.5% of the theoretical molecular space while deriving a physics-informed photostability model; multiple experimental test sets strengthened the model, and changing solvent triplet energy broke an optimization plateau in a hypothesis-directed validation.
candidates.scope: Photostability optimization and mechanistic inference in donor-acceptor molecules, with additional materials-system demonstrations. The 1.5% figure is coverage, not a universal speedup factor.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: Research loops should not optimize a scalar benchmark only; simultaneously fit interpretable mechanism models and schedule explicit hypothesis-breaking interventions. This could convert local optimization data into reusable knowledge and reduce repeated search across neighboring tasks.
candidates.confidence: high for original mechanism; medium for transfer

candidates.mechanism: Failure-inducing input minimization by repeated controlled deletion/partition tests (delta debugging), shrinking a complex failure to a minimal reproducer.
candidates.primary_source: Murphy system empirical application, USENIX ATC 2012, https://pages.cs.wisc.edu/~liblit/atc-2012/atc-2012.pdf ; delta debugging lineage Zeller/Hildebrandt
candidates.quantitative_evidence: In one reported Perl failure, delta debugging reduced a gremlin activation log from 114,019 interleaved read/write system calls to a single vulnerable call sufficient to reproduce the failure.
candidates.scope: Software fault localization under reproducible perturbation/replay. A single dramatic case is not an average-case speedup estimate.
candidates.transfer_hypothesis: When an experimental/reasoning pipeline fails, automatically minimize the causal context (tools, prompts, memory items, transformations, data slices) until a small reproducer remains, then use that as a high-information target for repair rather than debugging the whole trajectory.
candidates.confidence: medium-high for original mechanism; medium for transfer

rejected_or_deferred.reason: Too broad and likely redundant with well-known optimization practice; deferred unless a matched baseline or a structurally distinct mechanism is found.
Conceptually promising but this run did not obtain a clean primary empirical effect size comparable enough for promotion. Keep as frontier.
Broad autonomy descriptions are not themselves transferable mechanisms; only specific quantitatively supported submechanisms should be promoted.

frontier: Find primary quantitative evidence for dual control / active system identification showing the value of actions chosen partly for information gain under closed-loop control.
Investigate OCBA / ranking-and-selection from simulation optimization for explicit sample-allocation efficiency versus equal allocation.
Investigate adaptive checkpointing / straggler mitigation mechanisms distinct from request hedging, with matched overhead and tail-completion measurements.
Investigate experimental-design methods that optimize knowledge transfer across task families rather than one-task objective optimization.
Search software-engineering causal-debugging methods beyond delta debugging that quantify reduction in diagnosis trials or localization entropy.

termination_diagnostics.action_taken_instead_of_stopping: After obtaining racing/portfolio/work-stealing/closed-loop-transfer evidence, branched into software debugging and extracted a quantified delta-debugging failure-minimization case.

exact_next_action: Search primary OCBA / ranking-and-selection papers for a matched equal-allocation baseline and extract the smallest verified simulation-budget ratio or probability-of-correct-selection gain; if primary evidence is weak, branch to dual-control active identification experiments.
